agent_notes: STEPBible glosses ragal 'he takes slander'. The verb is a denominative from regel 'foot' (to go about on foot, to spy). I glossed it as 'he has gone about' and rendered it 'he has not gone about' in the literal layer. The lexical derivation is my own reading; Rashi and Ibn Ezra tie it only to the same verb in 2 Samuel 19:28.

agent_notes: The five English versions split on nivzeh ... nim'as. KJV, ASV and Webster take 'a vile person' as the one despised; BBE turns it into the man who gives honour. Both nivzeh and nim'as are Niphal participles with no noun, so 'a despised one' could also be read as the man himself (so Ibn Ezra, Radak, Meiri: he is lowly in his own eyes). I follow the grammar and the parallel with the next clause: the despised, rejected one is the person he rejects, set against those who fear YHWH.

I could not source the claim that 'to do harm' (lehara') means harm to himself; the Hebrew has no 'his own'. Rashi and Radak supply it, and the KJV adds 'his own' in italics. I mark it in brackets in the literal layer.

history.note: [consider] Rephrase to say the KJV takes nim'as as a noun ('a vile person') and nivzeh as its predicate; consider 'He has sworn' in the literal layer to match the gloss. (PS.15.4 KJV: "In whose eyes a vile person is contemned"; Hebrew "נִשְׁבַּע" (HVNp3ms).)

agent_notes: 'Coin' is gone from the commentary: kesef is silver, weighed out, with no reference to coinage. The commentary on the price of loans in a farm economy is my own reading, not a cited source; Radak's view that interest is forbidden only between Israelites is reported as his.

agent_notes: Игру ra'ah / re'ehu и звукопись ragal 'al leshono по-русски не воспроизвести; она объяснена в комментарии через транслитерацию. «Искреннему» в Синодальном переводе соответствует re'ehu (его ближний); в буквальном слое — «его другу/ближнему», «его близкому» для qarov.

Синодальный текст процитирован точно: «кто клянётся, хотя бы злому, и не изменяет»; утверждение о «своём вреде» убрано. «Хотя бы злому» отмечено как третье прочтение lehara' (клятва, данная злому человеку).

If you like, note instead that «хотя бы злому» reads lehara' as an oath made to a wicked man, a third reading.
